layout/index.md: "In Flutter, almost everything is a widget—even layout models are widgets. The images, icons, and text that you see in a Flutter app are all widgets." architectural-overview.md: "Widgets form a hierarchy based on composition. Each widget nests inside its parent"; "There are widgets for padding, alignment, rows, columns, and grids." Lesson now says "almost everything", matching the docs.

ui/index.md: "When a widget's state changes, the widget rebuilds its description, which the framework diffs against the previous description in order to determine the minimal changes needed in the underlying render tree to transition from one state to the next." Lesson's "works out the smallest set of changes between the two, and applies only those to the screen" matches; "to the screen" stands in for "render tree", acceptable under depth_notes (no RenderObject). Round-1 major resolved.

android-devs.md: "Flutter's widgets are lightweight, in part due to their immutability." ui/index.md: "...that operation is cheap because the framework compares the newly built widgets with the previously built widgets and applies only the differences". faq.md: "...efficiently handling small, short-lived allocations."

Analogy limited to containment. Supported by: "Widgets form a hierarchy based on composition. Each widget nests inside its parent and can receive context from the parent." The lesson's arrow gloss ("points from a widget to one it contains") holds as ancestor-to-descendant; framework widgets in between are not denied.

FutureBuilder: "Creates a widget that builds itself based on the latest snapshot of interaction with a [Future]." _FutureBuilderState._subscribe: `widget.future!.then((T data) { ... setState(() { _snapshot = AsyncSnapshot<T>.withData(ConnectionState.done, data); }); })`. AsyncSnapshot.data: "The latest data received by the asynchronous computation." The setState is in FutureBuilder's own state, so only FutureBuilder rebuilds; lesson §5 now says only that 'it builds again', and §6 no longer ties the title bar to this rebuild.

I can narrate the diagram only after the next section, which names every box in the same order, so this is minor.

issues.text: The first block uses `ApiClient` and `BuildContext context`, and the prose explains neither. From the name I guess ApiClient calls the backend and is handed to the screen, and I can skip `context`, but I have to stop to decide that.
issues.fix: Add one clause after the block, e.g. '`ApiClient` is the class that calls the API; the screen receives it as a constructor argument. Ignore `context` for now.'

issues.quote: `ProductListScreen` describes its page in a companion class, `_ProductListScreenState`; a later lesson explains why some widgets need one. That class's `build` returns a `Scaffold`, the standard page layout.
issues.text: I read this paragraph twice. It has MaterialApp's name and colours, what its title is not, `home`, a companion class and a Scaffold, all in three sentences. I followed it on the second read.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph after '…is a `ProductListScreen`.' so the companion-class sentence starts a new paragraph that names the file it is in (`product_list_screen.dart`).

issues.quote: and the title bar stays as it was while the body changes.
issues.text: Misconception 2 now points at something I can do (press refresh). But if Flutter really did redraw every pixel, the title bar would look exactly the same too. So what I see does not tell the two ideas apart, and 'You notice this when' promises evidence that I cannot see.
issues.fix: Either name something on screen that only the 'apply only the changes' version would show, or change 'You notice this when' to wording that says this is how to think about it, not something visible.
